result:
I’ll trace the invite form and batch endpoint, then add row feedback and a batch validation check. I’ll keep verification to inspection and focused static checks, as requested.
The two screens share the invite logic and batch endpoint. I found that the backend checks membership while saving each row, which allows earlier rows to be sent before a later one fails. I’ll move that check ahead of the save loop and use the same membership rule in the form. I’m applying the repository’s UI, copy, API, and test guidance for these edits.
The shared row can show the warning in both screens, but the normal member list may hide some teammates based on organization settings. I’ll use an invite-permitted email check for row feedback. The submit endpoint will still validate independently so a stale client check cannot let a partial batch through.
The backend now validates membership before saving any invite in the batch. The form checks the entered email against organization membership and shows the result on the row; the submit path also handles a membership change that happens after the form check. I’ve added focused regression cases for the late-row batch failure and error reporting. I won’t run them, per your request.
Implemented the invite validation change in both onboarding and organization settings. The shared invite row now flags your own email immediately and checks other entered emails when you leave the field, so you can change or remove an existing member before submitting.

The backend now checks membership during validation of the full batch, before any invite is created or emailed. Expected `already_member` rejections no longer produce a generic invite toast or error-tracking report. I added focused regression tests for a third-row failure and the email check.

I did not run tests or install dependencies, as requested. Python syntax checks passed. OpenAPI generation and TypeScript checks remain unrun because this checkout lacks their installed tooling.

```python
    def validate_target_email(self, email: str):
        email = EmailNormalizer.normalize(email)
        reject_plus_addressed_email(email)
        validate_invite_target_email_domain(self.context["get_organization"](), email)
        if OrganizationMembership.objects.filter(
            organization_id=self.context["organization_id"], user__email__iexact=email
        ).exists():
            raise exceptions.ValidationError(
                "A user with this email address already belongs to the organization.", code="already_member"
            )
        return email
```
